notes: Dev ABox revision whose edited relation carries transitivity. belongs_to_language_group (staged: transitive, asymmetric, inverse includes_language) holds between a language and each group it sits in (branch, family). The edit moves Hungarian from the Finno-Ugric branch (Uralic family) into the Slavic branch of Indo-European; families are disjoint, so the Uralic membership goes with it. Derived: transitivity (Slavic within Balto-Slavic), a composition that looks up a stored fact about the new branch itself (its proto-language, Proto-Slavic), and a binding through the endonym 'Magyar'. The direct, paraphrase, cross-lingual and binding questions ask the branch level explicitly ('at the level of Germanic or Romance'), since belongs_to_language_group is many-valued and transitive and an unqualified 'which group' would also be answered fairly by Indo-European or Balto-Slavic after the edit. Unrelated near asks Finnish, Hungarian's best-known relative; an edit that drags the family along would answer Slavic there. Related (one question): whether Hungarian and Estonian belong to the same language family (yes, then no once Hungarian is Slavic; composition through the family of Estonian, 2 hops, a fact about a different language). The formal file encodes it as Hungarian's membership in Uralic, with Estonian's membership a firm background fact. The first version asked the inverse (do the Finno-Ugric languages include Hungarian), which restated the edit.
